goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same problem: the second downsize definition overrides the first one.

goldens.comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
goldens.reasoning: C2 is a direct match: the hardcoded 10 MB ignores the per-type settings, and it also mentions the 413 handler. C4 covers the 413 handler part of the golden comment.

goldens.comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate raises the issue of gifsicle being given percentage dimensions.

goldens.comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate raises the issue of the loop using a stale tempfile size.

candidates: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 - Second `downsize` definition replaces the width/height version and breaks existing callers.. Ruby has no method overloading, so the new `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined just above it. Any existing call like `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 1000, 1000, allow_animation: ...)` now raises ArgumentError (5 for 3..4). A 4-argument call is worse: the height integer is taken as `opts`, so `opts[:allow_animation]` either raises or returns the wrong value. Either give the new method a different name (e.g. `downsize_by`), or have one method that accepts both forms.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 - Client size check now ignores the per-type site settings, including attachments.. `maxSizeKB` was `max_<type>_size_kb` and is now a fixed 10 MB for every upload type, attachments included. The request only covers downsizing images. If an admin set `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10 MB, users can no longer upload files the site allows. If it is set below 10 MB, the client lets files through that the server will reject. Line 246 has the same problem: the 413 message always reports 10 MB. Keep the site setting for non-image types and use a separate, larger limit only for images that will be downsized.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 - URL downloads are capped at a hardcoded 10 MB for every type.. The download cap used to be `max_image_size_kb`. Now it is a fixed 10 MB for images and attachments alike. On a site whose `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` is above 10 MB, the API can no longer fetch files the site allows: `FileHelper.download` fails, the error is rescued to nil, and the request then fails on a nil tempfile. Use `[10.megabytes, the relevant setting in kilobytes].max` instead of the constant.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 - The 413 error message always says the limit is 10 MB.. A 413 comes from the web server's own body limit, so it is unrelated to this hardcoded 10 MB. Before, the message at least showed the site setting. Now it can tell users the limit is 10 MB when the real limit is something else.
